title: Trace on a Karoubi summand
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: in particular $\ell\neq p$, a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$. The framework coefficient category $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] has objects $(E,K_E)$ at finite coefficient stages and morphisms represented at a common finite stage. Its idempotent completeness is the assertion of [lem-weil-qbar-idempotent-complete]; no extra idempotent is part of an object of $\mathcal C_X$. If one uses its formal Karoubi envelope [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], an object is $((E,K_E),e)$, where $e$ is an idempotent of $\mathcal C_X$.

For the trace construction, let $P\in\operatorname{Perf}(E)\subset D(E)$ be a perfect complex of ordinary $E$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and let $e:P\to P$ satisfy $e^2=e$. An endomorphism of the Karoubi object $(P,e)$ is represented by a morphism $u:P\to P$ satisfying $u=e\circ u\circ e$, as in [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. Define its *summand trace* by
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}_{E,(P,e)}(u):=\operatorname{tr}_E(u\circ e\mid P)\in E.
$$
Here $\operatorname{tr}_E$ is the categorical trace of [sk-d-trace], applied to the symmetric monoidal category of perfect $E$-complexes, with unit $E[0]$ and dual $P^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_E(P,E)$. Explicitly it is the composite
$$
 E[0]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_P}P\otimes_E^L P^\vee
 \xrightarrow{(u\circ e)\otimes1}P\otimes_E^L P^\vee
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{sym}}P^\vee\otimes_E^L P
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_P}E[0],
$$
read in $\operatorname{End}_{D(E)}(E[0])\cong E$ as in [sk-d-trace]. The equation $u=eue$ implies $ue=eu=u$, so the defining value is also $\operatorname{tr}_E(u\mid P)$.

Equivalently, for an ambient endomorphism $v:P\to P$ commuting with $e$, the induced endomorphism of $(P,e)$ is $u=eve=ve=ev$, and its summand trace is exactly the source formula $\operatorname{tr}_E(v\circ e\mid P)$. For such a commuting $v$, a splitting $S\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{r}S$ with $ri=1_S$ and $ir=e$ identifies the notation $(eP,ev)$ with the summand carrying induced endomorphism $(S,rvi)$. The assertion that the defining trace depends only on this summand, together with comparison of finite-stage representatives, is a well-definedness property, rather than additional defining data; see prop-trf-karoubi-independence (forward reference).

Sources: the blueprint text is identical in master (order 2397) and main-20261015 (order 2741); I also read sk-d-trace/_section.md and the unit sk-thm-trace-transport, whose Step 4 this item serves. I read the full statement of all 7 stmt_deps and checked each against its use. def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients gives C_X as pairs (E,K_E) with common-stage morphisms and no Karoubi completion. lem-weil-qbar-idempotent-complete is about that same framework category. The proper-base-change coefficient model is no longer identified with it. def-weil-karoubi-envelope gives u=eue with identity e. def-pc-perfect-ring-complex applies with R=E. sk-d-trace gives the coev/sym/ev composite on Perf(R) for any commutative R, with values in R. Replacing def-trf-categorical-trace was correct: that node, including its update, covers only A_{E,n}, so it cannot give an E-valued trace, and no other general trace node exists in the DAG. The algebra holds: u=eue implies ue=eu=u, and if ve=ev then eve=ve. The splitting order ri=1, ir=e is correct. The source's block-decomposition sentence is false for a v that does not commute with e: with e=diag(1,0) and v=[[0,0],[1,0]], ve=v but ev=0. The repair loses nothing, because the definition covers every Karoubi endomorphism; also tr(ve)=tr(eve) by cyclicity. No target or unit statement changes. Small cases check out: e=0, e=1, P=0, diagonal v, and the odd-degree Koszul sign. The forward reference to prop-trf-karoubi-independence correctly avoids a cycle, and the dependency closure (10,749 nodes) does not contain the item. No duplicate exists in the DAG, Mathlib has no categorical or Karoubi trace, the TeX is clean and no SGA source is cited. I made no changes.
